7.0.0.en: "In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head upon his bed:

7.0.1.en: then he wrote the dream, and told the sum of the matters." [1].

7.0.2.en: Daniel was granted this vision during the first year of the reign of Belshazzar, the last king of Babylon (556-539 B.C.); so historically this chapter comes before chapters [5-6]; that is, the time of this vision is the year 555 B.C.

7.1.1.en: "I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea." [2].

7.1.2.en: At night, that is, in this world before the Sun of righteousness has risen upon it, in the darkness of corruption that has no light, he saw the great sea, which we now call the Mediterranean Sea. 1. The boundary of the four great kingdoms was the Mediterranean Sea, and the capital of the last kingdom, "Rome," came on its shore, so it is fitting that the four beasts appear rising from it. 2. The sea in the Holy Bible refers symbolically to peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues (Rev 17:15; Lk 21:25; Isa 57:20). 3. The great sea with its waves symbolizes the state of constant disturbance or instability... This is a feature shared by the four kingdoms.

7.1.3.en: Some see that the great sea here is not the Mediterranean Sea as in (Josh 9:1), but the abyss, the dwelling of the devil, who in every generation sends his servants to work for the sake of his kingdom, and to resist the Kingdom of God. The sea also represents disturbance, for the kingdom of the enemy of good is built on spreading the spirit of disturbance and anxiety; therefore in the new heaven and the new earth there is no more sea (Rev 21:1).

7.1.4.en: The Jews see that the dragon, a symbol of the devil, dwells in the sea (Isa 27:1). And that the Church, awakened and clothed with strength, working with the arm of the Lord, dries up the sea and pierces the dragon: "Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD... Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon?" (Isa 51:9-10). Therefore she sings, saying: "Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters. Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces" (Ps 74:13-14).

7.2.0.en: They refer to God's hidden agencies at work. The wind also refers to the Holy Spirit who works in secret (Jn 3:8), since "wind" and "spirit" are one word in Hebrew as in Greek. It is as though what the prophet sees here proceeds from heaven by divine permission, where the Spirit of God works for the sake of His heavenly Kingdom even if events seem bitter or resistant to the work of God.

7.2.1.en: * I think that the four winds of heaven are angelic powers to which the principalities were entrusted, in agreement with what is said in the book of Deuteronomy: "When the Most High divided to the nations, when He separated the sons of Adam, He set boundaries for peoples according to the number of the angels; the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" (Deut 32:8) LXX. But the sea means this world and the present time, covered by the salty, bitter waves, as the Lord's interpretation of the net cast into the sea (Mt 13). So also the king of all the creatures dwelling in the waters is described as a dragon, whose heads are struck in the sea, as David says (Ps 73). And we read in Amos: "And though he hide in the depths of the sea, thence will I command the dragon, and it shall bite him" (Amos 9:3) LXX... As for the four winds that blow upon the great sea, they are called "winds of heaven" because each angel practices within the limits of his jurisdiction what he is bound to do.

7.2.2.en: St. Jerome Perhaps by the four winds of heaven he means that what will happen concerning the four empires is at the mercy of the wind; kingdoms carry no stability, and it is not in the hand of any man to change the events that God declares to him.

7.3.0.en: 3 And four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another. 4 The first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings:

7.3.1.en: I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man's heart was given to it. [3-4].

7.4.0.en: In [17] the four beasts refer to four kings, while in [23] the fourth beast refers to the fourth kingdom. It is clear that each of the kingdoms was known by a particular king who had his chief role in the kingdom as a whole. Nebuchadnezzar represents the kingdom of Babylon, while Cyrus represents the kingdom of Persia, and Alexander the Great represents the Greek (Macedonian) kingdom, while the Roman kingdom is referred to in the book of Revelation as the beast (Rev 13).

7.4.1.en: The kingdom of Babylon is referred to as a winged lion, that is, distinguished by strength and predation with swiftness of movement, since the Babylonian state almost took possession of the whole world in a short period. In Ezekiel 17 Babylon is referred to as the flying eagle, which snatches its prey swiftly, and no one can catch up with it. St. Jerome says: [As for the fact that it has the wings of an eagle, this refers to the pride of the all-powerful kingdom, and of the ruler referred to in Isaiah: "I will exalt my throne above the stars of heaven, I will be like the Most High" (Isa 14:14). Therefore it was said: "Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle... thence will I bring thee down" (Num 4). Moreover, just as the lion holds a royal rank among the beasts, so the eagle holds it among the birds].

7.4.2.en: The prophet Daniel beheld the Babylonian kingdom with its wings plucked, standing upon the earth; that is, it began to collapse, as it became unable to fly.

7.4.3.en: When a man is known for his courage it is said of him, "Lion-hearted," like King Richard, but here we find a lion with the heart of a man. Outwardly it appears a courageous lion among the beasts, and inwardly it is full of fear like an unarmed man among predatory beasts. This is what happened to Babylon in the days of Belshazzar.

7.4.4.en: St. Jerome translates the Aramaic word aryeh as a lioness, in the feminine. And he says: [The kingdom of the Babylonians was not called a lion but a "lioness," because of its savagery and cruelty, or rather because of its luxury and a life marked by indulgence in lusts]. He also says: [The writers of natural history affirm that lionesses are fiercer than lions, especially when they are nursing leopards, and they are always lustful in sexual relations].

7.4.6.en: [When he speaks of a lioness rising from the sea, he means the rise of the kingdom of Babylon, which is the very head of the golden statue. As for the mention of the wings of an eagle, it means King Nebuchadnezzar who exalted himself and was proud in his glory against God. Then it was said "its wings were plucked," that is, his glory was shattered, when he was driven out from his kingdom. And the words "and a man's heart was given to it, and it was made to stand upon two feet as a man" mean that he returned to himself and knew that he was merely a man, giving glory to God].

7.4.8.en: [If we understand that of Nebuchadnezzar, it is very clear that after he lost his kingdom his strength was taken from him, and then he was restored to his original state and learned not only to be a man instead of a lioness, but also to recover the heart he had lost. On the other hand it can be understood and applied to the kingdom of the Chaldeans in general, which means that after the killing of Belshazzar, when the Medes and Persians took the imperial authority, the men of Babylon realized that their nature is feebler and lowlier than all].

7.5.0.en: a. It was founded by Nabopolassar I after he rebelled against the kingdom of Assyria in the north and became independent of it and formed the new kingdom of Babylon. And in 612 B.C. he destroyed Nineveh and burned it.

7.5.1.en: b. Nebuchadnezzar (606-562), who made many conquests, and founded the city of Babylon and the temples of Marduk, and invaded Jerusalem three times (606, 599, 587 B.C.). The last time he destroyed the temple and burned it and laid waste Jerusalem, so the continual burnt offering was stopped for the whole period of the captivity.

7.5.2.en: c. And Evil-merodach (562-560 B.C.), who pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah.

7.5.3.en: d. Nergal-sharezer (560-556 B.C.), who was the husband of the sister of the previous king.

7.5.4.en: e. Nabonidus, the father of Belshazzar (556-539 B.C.), in whose days the Babylonian state came to an end. He abdicated the kingship to his son, and when Cyrus invaded Babylon he killed Belshazzar and spared his father, who was most likely outside the city of Babylon, and he remained withdrawn from political work until the day of his death.

7.6.s.en: 4. The second beast: the Medes and Persians:

7.6.0.en: And behold another beast, a second, like to a bear, and it raised up itself on one side, and it had three ribs in the mouth of it between the teeth of it: and they said thus unto it,

7.6.2.en: The most important features of the bear are its strength and ferocity along with its cowardice. The kingdom of Persia and Media was known not to have defeated its enemies through military skill and speed of movement, but by invading countries with huge numbers of fighters; in the war of Ahasuerus against the Greeks he fought with about 2.5 million fighters, besides 2.5 million of his allied subjects, so his camp numbered about 5 million, and whenever they entered a city they caused it destruction because of the great number, and caused famines because they seized the food supplies for the needs of the army.

7.6.3.en: It raised itself on one side, because the kingdom consists of two nations, the Medes who are older, and after them the Persians, but after a short time Persia gained control over Media. St. Jerome sees that the bear's raising itself on one side indicates that the kingdom of Persia, although fierce with the peoples, was gentle with the Jews. It treated the other peoples in one way and the Jews in another way, that is, it stands on one side.

7.6.4.en: The three ribs between its teeth are the main Babylonian cities, Babylon, Ecbatana, and Borsippa. These cities were opened by the armies of Cyrus. Or they may refer to the kingdoms it devoured: Lydia, Babylon, and Egypt. St. Hippolytus of Rome sees that they refer to three nations: "the Medes, the Persians, and Babylon," which came together under the banner of the Persian Empire.

7.7.s.en: As for the kings of Persia, they are:

7.7.0.en: a. Cyrus II (559-530 B.C.), whom the prophet Isaiah called "Cyrus the Lord's anointed," because he pardoned the Jews and issued a decree for the first return from the captivity of Babylon in the days of Zerubbabel and his permission to him to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem, and he gave back to them all the vessels of the temple that Nebuchadnezzar had plundered. This Cyrus had begun his reign in the northern part in 559 B.C., but he was able to annex Babylon, which is the southern part, in 539 B.C., after he defeated Belshazzar the last king of Babylon, who at that time was carrying out new conquests in the Arabian Peninsula.

7.7.2.en: c. The one called Smerdis-Pseudo (522 B.C.).

7.7.4.en: e. Ahasuerus I (Xerxes I) (486-465 B.C.), the book of Esther.

7.7.5.en: f. Artaxerxes I (465-424 B.C.), the book of Nehemiah.

7.8.s.en: 5. The third beast: the Greek Empire:

7.8.0.en: After this I beheld, and lo another, like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl;

7.8.1.en: the beast had also four heads; and dominion was given to it. [6].

7.8.2.en: Though it is smaller than the lion in size, it has four wings and four heads.

7.8.3.en: If the Greek Empire was less than the Babylonian Empire, as the leopard is smaller than the lion, yet Alexander the Great was more mobile and swifter than the Babylonian emperors, so four wings appeared on the leopard, like one flying to all four directions of the world.

7.8.4.en: The four wings refer to a doubled swiftness of movement and victory, for in about ten years Alexander the Great, the founder of the Greek Empire, defeated the forces of Persia in 333 B.C., and subdued the whole world extending at that time, including Egypt and Palestine, and the four heads refer to the division of the kingdom into four parts after the death of Alexander the Great at the age of thirty-four, directly among his four commanders: Seleucus, who became king over Syria, and Ptolemy, who reigned over Egypt, Israel, and Palestine. The third reigned over Macedonia, and the fourth over Thrace.

7.8.5.en: And as St. Jerome says: [No victory was ever swifter than that of Alexander, for he crossed the whole way from Illyricum and the Adriatic Sea to the Indian Ocean and the river Ganges, not merely entering into battle but gaining decisive, mighty victories, and in six years he subjugated to his rule a portion of Europe and all of Asia].

7.8.6.en: With his sharp intelligence and military abilities, what he achieved was only because authority was given to him from God. And as St. Jerome says: [By the words "and dominion was given to it" it is shown that the empire did not arise as the fruit of Alexander's courage but by the will of God].

7.9.s.en: 6. The fourth beast: the Roman Empire:

7.9.0.en: 7 After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.

7.9.1.en: The discussion of the Roman Empire occupies the largest share of the chapter. Unlike the previous beasts, it was symbolized by a beast to which the prophet Daniel saw no likeness and of which he had not heard, for in the world of predatory beasts there is nothing that bears the mark of ferocity and violence like this empire.

7.9.2.en: St. Jerome says: [We saw in the previous beasts various symbols of terror, but all of these are concentrated in this one beast].

7.9.3.en: He also says: [Perhaps this was to show the beast in a terrifying form; in truth He gave it no name, so that we may understand from this that the Romans shared in the most hideous traits of ferocity that we can think of with regard to beasts... They are like a beast that devours and crushes and tramples all the rest with its feet. This means that the Romans either slaughter the nations or subject them to tribute and slavery].

7.9.4.en: The kingdom of the Romans began from the year 63 B.C. and its conquests extended until it occupied the lands of the old kingdoms of Babylon and Persia and Egypt in the year 47 B.C.

7.9.5.en: "After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth:

7.9.6.en: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it:

7.9.7.en: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it;

7.9.9.en: This beast is stronger than the previous beasts: "dreadful, and strong, and exceeding terrible, with teeth of iron and claws of brass" (the Septuagint). It corresponds to the feet of the statue which Nebuchadnezzar saw, "his feet part of iron and part of clay" (Dan 2:33). St. Hippolytus of Rome says that the ten toes of the feet, some of which were of iron and the others of clay, correspond to the ten horns of this beast, and they refer symbolically to the ten kings who arose from this kingdom.

7.9.10.en: This beast was described as dreadful and strong and exceeding terrible, because it cannot be compared with the former kingdoms. It is true that Alexander the Great subdued most of the countries of the world, but he sought fame, not domination, and when his dreams were fulfilled he granted the countries subject to him much freedom. But the Romans subdued the world and became its violent masters. They subdued Asia Minor, Syria, Cilicia, Greece, Macedonia, Spain, Gaul, and part of Germany. All the countries of the Mediterranean Sea were subject to it. It is true that Egypt had its kings, but they were subject to tribute; and every law the Romans issued was applied immediately in Egypt. They left governors in Asia Minor, but they were spies for the Romans. Julius Caesar was the first to enter Britain after subduing Gaul, etc. For all this Daniel called it the dreadful, strong, and exceeding terrible beast.

7.9.11.en: "And it had great iron teeth" [7], an indication of its violent predation with its intense greed. The best crops and resources of the world were transported to Rome, without its being satisfied. The empire was not concerned with the needs of the colonized countries but crushed them and trampled them with its feet. The emperors used to send their ambassadors to the countries under the pretext of preserving the security and peace of the state, and their first concern was spying on behalf of the emperors, and transporting everything valuable to them.

7.9.12.en: Some modern critics think that this beast refers to the Seleucids, and its ten heads are the kings: Seleucus I, Antiochus Soter, Antiochus II, Seleucus II, Seleucus III, Antiochus III, Seleucus IV, Heliodorus, Ptolemy VI, Demetrius, and the mighty horn is Antiochus Epiphanes who trampled the last three kings. But the more probable opinion is that the fourth beast refers to the Roman Empire. It is a strange beast with no likeness, because the Roman state did not impose its culture on the countries it colonized. All that concerned it was military authority and the collection of tribute. It was distinguished by administration and organization and did not care about any particular cultural thought, so the state came to hold diverse cultures, each country according to its own desire.

7.9.13.en: Some see in the ten horns a reference to the ten persecutions that the Romans practiced against the Church, and others see that they represent kingdoms that would come into being during the second stage of the history of the beast. It does not necessarily follow that these kingdoms must arise after the weakening of Rome. All that can be concluded from this is that these kingdoms can be traced back to Rome, and they are contemporary only in the sense of existing in a certain period, so it is not necessary that they be contemporary in fact.

7.9.14.en: Some of the Jews thought that it means here the rising of ten kings ruling together in Rome, but it is clear that the number 10 in the Holy Bible means multitude, for the Roman emperors appointed many governors over their colonies, a governor over Syria and another over Macedonia and a third over Spain, etc. And they had rights similar to the rights of kings, doing as they wished, but they were subject to the emperor and obeyed his laws that he issued, who counted himself king of kings or like a god.

7.10.0.en: I considered the horns, and, behold, there came up among them another little horn, before whom there were three of the first horns plucked up by the roots: and, behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of man, and a mouth speaking great things. [8].

7.10.1.en: In the opinion of Porphyry the little horn that appeared after the ten horns is Antiochus Epiphanes, and the three horns that were plucked up from the ten are Ptolemy VI (Philometer), Ptolemy VII (Euergetes), and Artaraxias king of Armenia.

7.10.2.en: St. Jerome rejected this interpretation, saying: [Some Christian interpreters have said that it is the devil or some satan, or perhaps a man over whom Satan has entirely reigned, the son of sin, the son of perdition, who dares to sit in the temple of God, making himself like God (2 Thess 2).

7.11.0.en: He also says that if the little horn were Antiochus whom Judas Maccabeus defeated, can it be said of Judas that he comes on the clouds as a son of man [13], and that he is presented before "the Ancient of days" [13], and how is it said of him that he is given dominion and royal power and that all peoples, tribes, and tongues worship him and that his dominion is eternal and does not end [14]?. [If it refers to the Maccabees, let the defenders of this position explain how the kingdom of the Maccabees has the character of permanence [14].

7.11.1.en: John Calvin mentions in his commentary on the book of Daniel that in his days some thought that the little horn is the pope of Rome or the appearance of the Turks, and he rejected this opinion. He proclaimed that Julius Caesar and the Caesars who followed him, that is, Augustus, Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius, Nero, and others, are the little horn, proving this by the fact that these Caesars, with all the authority they had, shared the authority with the council of nobles, the senate, which limited their authority, and for this reason they were called the little horn.

7.11.2.en: If the visions and prophecies aimed at revealing the coming of the Lord Christ to establish His spiritual Kingdom in hearts, shattering violence from the heart, then the enemy of good does not stand with folded hands but resists the Lord. This resistance is manifested in its most hideous form in the last days when the Antichrist comes, or the man of sin, or the false prophet. This is what the prophet Daniel prophesied here under the symbol of "the little horn," as the Lord Christ spoke to us of him clearly and plainly in His discourse about the end of the times (Mt 24), and also St. Paul (2 Thess 3:8), and St. John the Seer (Rev 13).

7.11.3.en: The little horn here refers to the Antichrist. The Old Testament spoke of him as did the New Testament (Mt 24; 2 Thess 2:2-8; Rev 13; Dan 7), to affirm that even though the Church lives in severe tribulation, especially in the last days, there is a divine plan that ends in the victory of the Kingdom of God. However much the devil and all his soldiers resist, the saints will certainly reign with God, not on a passing earth but in the heavenlies. The description of the Antichrist here corresponds to what is stated in the New Testament.

7.11.4.en: As for the features of this little horn, they are:

7.11.5.en: a. Small, mysterious, and violent [8], he appears suddenly, and shatters kingdoms, and sets up for himself a kingdom that resists the Church of God [25], because of him great terror occurs [28].

7.11.6.en: b. He rises as another king [8], subject to death (Rev 13:2; 2 Thess 2:9), bearing satanic power, making himself a god.

7.11.7.en: c. His power begins with the overthrow of three kings [8, 24].

7.11.8.en: d. Intelligent and deceitful, he knows how to plan... he has many eyes.

7.11.9.en: e. A blasphemer, he resists God, and has the ability to speak [8].

7.13.0.en: g. His kingdom is passing, lasting only a time, two times, and half a time. He thinks that he will shatter the Kingdom of God and change the times and seasons [25], as though he did not know of the existence of a hidden divine plan that shatters all his evil.

7.13.1.en: h. The secret of the victory over him is the coming of the Lord Christ: 1. The first coming: where He shattered the work of the devil by His Cross. 2. The second coming: that His saints may reign with Him in heaven after the shattering of the Antichrist. 3. The coming of the Lord into the heart to shatter the kingdom of evil within.

7.14.0.en: 9 I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit,

7.14.1.en: whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire. 10 A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him:

7.14.2.en: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him:

7.14.3.en: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. 11 I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake:

7.14.4.en: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame. 12 As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time. [9-12].

7.15.0.en: After speaking of the four empires that ended with the coming of the Lord Christ to establish His Kingdom over hearts, he spoke of the judgment of these fierce empires, for he saw the eternal God sitting on the throne, having cast down the thrones of the empires also and taken away their authority, even though He gave them "length of life for a season and time" [12].

7.15.1.en: He speaks here of God as Judge, calling Him "the Ancient of days," to affirm that nothing of past events escapes His eyes. He is the eternal Judge, but in His longsuffering He awaits the appropriate time. From the beginning of our creation He gives us opportunities to enjoy His mercies, and from our fall He watches for our return to Him, but a time comes when He sits on the throne of judgment to judge with justice and righteousness.

7.15.2.en: Some see that the expression "thrones were placed" in Hebrew means "thrones were removed" of kings and great men so that the King of kings, who alone has the right to judge, may sit. Yet some see that the meaning here is "thrones were set up," where God sits and around Him the heavenly ones watch the judgment, and rejoice at the victory of the believers and the shattering of the devil and all his soldiers.

7.15.3.en: Perhaps the thrones here refer to the promise of the Lord Christ to His disciples that they will judge the children of Israel. For God, who is altogether just, judges humanity; He judges the righteous who overcome the wicked who are without excuse, rebuking them by the righteousness of their fellow servants who lived with them in this world.

7.15.4.en: The description of God the Judge here corresponds to what is said of the Lord Christ in Revelation (Rev 1:2-4 etc.)! And the Lord Christ spoke of Himself as Judge of the nations (Mt 25:30-46).

7.15.5.en: * The more a man hastens to the end, the more venerable he is, and God alone is greater than he, for He is the Eternal, the Ancient of days, older than everything.

7.15.6.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * If the one who is judged will undoubtedly be wretched, yet the one for whose sake God sits (to reward him) is happy.

7.15.7.en: * God's judgment comes to humble pride. For this reason the Roman state will perish, because it is the horn that speaks arrogant words.

7.15.8.en: St. Jerome * Because in the judgment of God that Daniel describes we find Him sitting, and he points to the books that were opened (Dan 7:10), without doubt these are the books that contain the sins of men. We ourselves write these documents that condemn us, by the things that we commit.

7.15.9.en: Origen We know that God cannot be seen as He is, but He reveals Himself as far as we are able to see Him, and in the way in which we are built. Here, since the vision presents the conflict between the kingdom of the Lord Christ in His saints and the kingdom of the Antichrist, God appears in a garment white as snow and the hair of His head like the pure wool. Whiteness and purity symbolize the heavenly life without defilement. It is as though our weapon in the battle is our enjoyment of the pure heavenly life. The lifting up of the heart to heaven, our occupation with eternal things, and the purity of our souls are our weapons on behalf of the kingdom of Christ.

7.15.10.en: As for the mention of the fiery, flaming throne and the burning fiery wheels, it means our duty that our depths be turned into a spiritual throne kindled with the fire of divine love, so that there is no place in us for sloth or slackness, but we are like the Cherubim burning with the fire of the Spirit.

7.15.11.en: From before Him comes forth a river of fire flowing abundantly, and it waters our souls not with water but with holy fire, so our depths are turned into a garden bearing the fruit of the fiery Spirit. If the Antichrist is terrifying and fearful, the children of God, upon whom the heavenly river overflows with surpassing fire, become terrifying, and the enemy cannot stand before them!

7.15.12.en: Finally he declares that countless multitudes stand before Him, thousand thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, longing to serve Him. In brief, the heavenly ones and the believers with them stand bearing the following marks:

7.15.14.en: * The flame of love and burning zeal.

7.15.15.en: * The fire of the bold heart that does not fail or feel shame.

7.15.17.en: Origen sees that the book of life or the divine book is mentioned in the singular, like that which St. John the Theologian saw, whose key is in the hands of the Lion that came out of the tribe of Judah (Rev 5:1-5; 3:7), the book of which Moses the prophet said: "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written" (Ex 32:32). While the plural form is used for the books in which those who are kept for judgment are recorded.

7.15.18.en: * The books, which are closed until that time, give an account of everything we do, every word we have spoken and every thought, even every idle word (Mt 12:36), all that is recorded in the books of God. Some think that there are real books in heaven in which our sins are engraved. I think that these books are our consciences, which will be revealed on that day, and each one will see what he has done for himself.

7.15.19.en: St. Jerome * The consciences of men and the deeds of individuals that contribute to every personality, whether good or evil, are disclosed before all. One of these books is the good book that we often read, I mean the book of the living. The other book is the evil book that the accuser holds in his hand, who is exceedingly vengeful and malicious, of whom we read in Revelation "the accuser of our brethren" (Rev 12:10). This is the earthly book of which the prophet says: "shall be written in the earth" (Jer 17:13).

7.16.s.en: 9. The likeness of a son of man:

7.16.0.en: 13 "I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. 14 And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him:

7.16.1.en: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed. [13-14].

7.16.2.en: He comes to reign forever, where the saints enjoy the fellowship of glory with Him. In the dialogue of Tertullian with the Jews he made clear that Daniel prophesied beforehand of two comings of the Lord Christ: He came first as a little stone that strikes the statue of the temporal kingdoms and shatters them, He came incarnate, emptying Himself, and at the second coming He comes in His royal heavenly glory on the clouds.

7.16.3.en: * He is the Son of God, our Lord, for He is the Word of the Father; and He is the Son of man, for He was born according to His humanity of Mary, so He descended from the human race, and He is a human being since He became the Son of man.

7.16.4.en: St. Irenaeus * All authority given by the Father to the Son has been shown, who was appointed Lord of all that is in heaven and on earth and under the earth and Judge of all (Phil 2:10).

7.16.5.en: He is Lord of those in heaven because He is the Word of God begotten before the ages; and Lord of those on earth because He was numbered among the dead, preaching the Gospel to the souls of the saints (1 Pet 3:19), and He conquered death by death.

7.17.0.en: At the beginning Daniel was greatly troubled about this vision, so he approached one of those who stood by, who was most likely an angel, asking him for an interpretation of what he was seeing. But Daniel came to enjoy peace after he realized that these kingdoms, in spite of the authority they receive and their ferocity, end with the kingdom of the saints in heaven, which is preceded by the great tribulation caused by the Antichrist. 15 "I Daniel was grieved in my spirit in the midst of my body, and the visions of my head troubled me. 16 I came near unto one of them that stood by, and asked him the truth of all this.

7.17.1.en: So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things. 17 These great beasts, which are four, are four kings, which shall arise out of the earth. 18 But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever. [15-18].

7.17.2.en: The prophet Daniel saw all the multitudes of the heavenly ones standing before the throne preparing to serve Him with joy, as he says: "thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him" (Dan 7:10), which stirs us to gather together after the pattern of the heavenly ones to serve God.

7.17.3.en: St. Clement of Rome says: [And we also, gathering together with one another in agreement, cry out earnestly as with one mouth, that we may become partakers of His great and glorious promises], [Let our boasting and our confidence be in the Lord, and let us submit to His will, and realize that all the multitudes of His angels stand around Him, ready to serve His will].

7.17.4.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that this picture stirs in us the longing to be like the angels through the saving work of Christ in us, so he says: [We live with Christ as a result of our crucifixion with Him, and we are also glorified with Him and reign with Him. The result of our presence before God is that we are changed from the rank of human nature and human dignity to that of the angels, and so Daniel says "thousand thousands stand before him"].

7.17.5.en: * It is very fitting for those who are white and without wrinkle within to use white and simple garments. Daniel says with all clarity and plainness: "The thrones were cast down and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow" [9]. And Revelation says that the Lord Himself appeared wearing such a garment, as it says: "I saw the souls of those who were martyred under the altar, and a white robe was given to each of them" (Rev 6:9, 11). And if there is a need to look for another color, the natural color of truth is sufficient.

7.18.s.en: 11. The kingdom of the Antichrist and the kingdom of the saints:

7.18.0.en: 19 Then I would know the truth of the fourth beast, which was diverse from all the others, exceeding dreadful, whose teeth were of iron, and his nails of brass; which devoured, brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with his feet; 20 And of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell; even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things, whose look was more stout than his fellows. 21 I beheld, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them; 22 Until the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom. 23 Thus he said, The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces. 24 And the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise: and another shall rise after them; and he shall be diverse from the first, and he shall subdue three kings. 25 And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time. 26 But the judgment shall sit, and they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end. 27 And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.

7.18.1.en: "Then I would know the truth of the fourth beast, which was diverse from all the others, exceeding dreadful, whose teeth were of iron, and his nails of brass; which devoured, brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with his feet; and of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell; even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things, whose look was more stout than his fellows.

7.18.2.en: "I beheld, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;

7.18.3.en: Until the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom" [19-21].

7.18.4.en: The prophet Daniel longed to learn the truth of this strange beast, different from the rest of the beasts, in order to grasp its mystery. He repeated its description because of his astonishment, and because he sensed the gravity of its role and its mad, deadly work.

7.19.0.en: The other king who comes after the ten kings is the little horn who is known as the Antichrist. This one reigns "until a time and times and the dividing of time" [20], or "a time, two times, and half a time." In the opinion of St. Jerome the time here means "a year," that is, the Antichrist reigns three and a half years [16-23].

7.19.1.en: * The Antichrist will stir up war against the saints and will overcome them, and will glorify himself to such a height of arrogance, trying to change the very laws of God and the holy rites also. He will exalt himself against all that is called God, subjecting those who are his.

7.19.2.en: * The four kingdoms of which he spoke before are earthly in their features. "All are of the dust, and all turn to dust again" (Eccl 3:20). But the saints will not receive an earthly kingdom, but only a heavenly one. Away with the trifling idea of the thousand-year kingdom!

7.19.3.en: St. Jerome "Thus he said, The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.

7.19.4.en: And the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise: and another shall rise after them; and he shall be diverse from the first, and he shall subdue three kings.

7.19.5.en: And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.

7.19.6.en: But the judgment shall sit, and they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end.

7.19.7.en: And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High,

7.20.0.en: whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him" [22-27].

7.21.0.en: Hitherto is the end of the matter.

7.21.1.en: As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me, and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart." [28].

7.21.2.en: The prophet Daniel declares his inability to grasp the full interpretation of the vision, therefore he kept the matter in his heart [28].

7.22.0.en: * Behold, the world is like a troubled sea, out of which come predatory beasts, devouring and dominating!

7.22.1.en: But Your Kingdom is surely coming!

7.22.2.en: You reign in Your saints forever!

7.22.3.en: Not on a passing earth, but in a new, immortal heaven!

7.22.5.en: You are surely coming to reign!

7.22.6.en: But the Antichrist enters the field of battle, it is a decisive battle, it is life or death!

7.22.7.en: Let evil die, and let darkness be abolished, and let the Kingdom of light be established within us!

7.22.8.en: * Let the Antichrist come, he is extremely violent and a destroyer of souls!

7.22.9.en: But You are stronger and greater.

7.22.10.en: Protect Your Church, for the end of the times has begun!
